items.followUp: A body weighing 15 N is raised vertically through 4 m. Calculate the potential energy stored in it.

rubric.why: The weight and vertical height are the given quantities needed for the calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the weight as 20 N and the height as 6 m.

rubric.why: Gravitational potential energy is the product of weight and vertical height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

rubric.why: The given weight and height must be substituted correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 20 N and 6 m into the formula.

rubric.why: The product of weight and height gives the stored potential energy in joules.
rubric.description: Calculates the potential energy and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 120 J; award 1 mark for the correct numerical answer without a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Weight, W = 20 N; height, h = 6 m.
Formula: P.E. = weight × height = W × h.

items.followUp: State Pascal’s Law and explain how a hydraulic jack multiplies force.

rubric.why: Pascal’s Law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.description: Identifies the applied pressure and enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is applied to an enclosed fluid.

rubric.why: These are the essential features of how the applied pressure is transmitted.
rubric.description: States how the pressure is transmitted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the pressure is transmitted undiminished in all directions.

rubric.why: The applied force on the smaller piston produces pressure in the liquid.
rubric.description: Explains the input side of the press.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that force on the small piston produces pressure, such as P = F1/A1.

rubric.why: Equal transmitted pressure acting on the larger piston produces a larger output force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the pressures and explaining that the larger piston produces a larger force.

modelAnswer: Pascal’s Law: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.
A hydraulic press has a small piston of area A1 and a large piston of area A2 connected by an enclosed liquid.
A force F1 on the small piston produces pressure P = F1/A1 in the liquid.
This pressure is transmitted to the large piston, so F2/A2 = F1/A1.
Since A2 > A1, F2 > F1; therefore, the press produces a larger output force.

items.followUp: Calculate the centripetal force on a 2 kg body moving at 4 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m.

rubric.why: The radius must be converted from centimetres to metres before substitution.
rubric.description: Identifies the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.50 m and v = 3 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: This is the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The mass, speed and converted radius must be substituted correctly with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution into the formula.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a centripetal force of 9 newtons.
rubric.description: Calculates the force and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 9 N; award 1 mark for the correct numerical result without a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg; r = 50 cm = 0.50 m; v = 3 m/s.
